# Phase Three — Tiferes Final Improvement Plan

> Chesed imagines endless cinema, Gevurah measures every cost, Tiferes joins the two in form;  
> the Awtsmoos renews each frame, while Awtsmoos.com makes speed and meaning one coherent storm.

## Third-Pass Revelation

The system does not need another movie schema, another Studio shell, or another proof-only workaround. It needs deeper engines that preserve the verified architecture:

- **Render:** faster orchestration around the existing deterministic renderer, with sequential equivalence and bounded memory proven.
- **AI:** richer canonical scene composition below the already-thin Director, with semantic coverage measured from actual generated layers.
- **Studio:** authoring feedback that surfaces richness, fidelity, and render quality without lying about native capabilities.

## 34 Additional Improvements Beyond Phase Two

1. Benchmark constructor cost separately from frame render cost.
2. Warm each renderer once before timing steady-state throughput.
3. Record median, p90, and max frame latency instead of a single average.
4. Benchmark multiple timestamps because some scenes/overlays are more expensive.
5. Compare buffer hashes between repeated sequential renders to prove determinism before parallelization.
6. Use a compact worker initialization payload rather than serializing unnecessary UI metadata.
7. Partition frame requests into small chunks when IPC per frame dominates.
8. Maintain an explicit maximum reorder-window size.
9. Apply backpressure from ffmpeg all the way to worker scheduling.
10. Terminate worker processes on cancellation and error; do not orphan native Canvas processes.
11. Include worker/frame identifiers in errors for reproducible diagnostics.
12. Add an automatic sequential fallback if worker initialization fails.
13. Make worker count injectable for deterministic tests.
14. Do not assume `os.availableParallelism()` cores should all be used; leave headroom for ffmpeg and the OS.
15. Benchmark 1, 2, and 4 workers before choosing defaults.
16. Preserve exact local-time calculations from the sequential exporter.
17. Avoid encoding per worker unless raw IPC is proven worse; encoding many tiny streams may cost more CPU.
18. Keep render benchmark artifacts out of production proof directories.
19. In AI planning, distinguish requested features from inferred enhancements.
20. Add `requestedCoverage` and `generatedCoverage` evidence to AI metadata only if schema allows arbitrary metadata cleanly.
21. Scene purposes should be deterministic from duration/genre but not repetitive round-robin labels without context.
22. Camera choices should vary by purpose and dimension, not merely scene index.
23. Character scenes need spatial/action beats, not just presence layers.
24. Infographic scenes need actual chart/label/data semantic layers.
25. Tutorial scenes need step/focus/annotation semantics and readable text.
26. Hybrid scenes should intentionally combine 2D overlays with 3D world/model/character layers.
27. Particle use should have semantic roles such as emphasis, transition, ambience, or visualization.
28. Text density must remain bounded for mobile readability.
29. Generated style should be stable across scenes through deterministic palette/motion choices.
30. Richness scoring should penalize missing requested features more strongly than lack of optional flair.
31. Tests should include negative prompts that request only simple 2D output to prove the planner does not force 3D everywhere.
32. Studio richness UI should summarize instead of exposing raw internal arrays by default.
33. Studio render presets should show FPS/dimensions and relative cost, never promise exact wall-clock completion.
34. Final acceptance must prove either measured render-throughput improvement or explicitly reject the parallel architecture with benchmark evidence before moving to micro-optimization.

## Final Execution Order

### Gate 0 — Collision / Reality Refresh

- Read current git status and modification times for renderer, AI compiler, Studio layout, and new plan directory.
- Identify any active concurrent movie agent touching the same files.
- If a candidate file changed after planning, re-read before deciding.

### Gate 1 — Baseline Benchmark

Read and benchmark `CinematicFrameRenderer` plus immediate dependencies. Create a small benchmark script only after reading current constructors/APIs. Baseline representative frames with one renderer instance. Record throughput and determinism hashes.

### Gate 2 — Parallel Prototype

If renderer isolation is valid, add new child-process worker modules without rewriting cinematic painting code. Benchmark 1/2/4 workers on a bounded frame set. Require correct ordered hashes and meaningful throughput improvement. If it loses, delete/avoid integrating the prototype and record why.

### Gate 3 — Export Integration

Only if Gate 2 wins, integrate the worker pool into a separate parallel exporter path. Keep sequential exporter as fallback. Verify a short higher-FPS movie/segment before attempting full 180 seconds.

### Gate 4 — AI Baseline

Read prompt/intent/outline compiler modules. Generate at least five prompt fixtures and inventory layer kinds, cameras, scene purposes, and requested-feature misses.

### Gate 5 — AI Richness Modules

Create small deterministic planners/factories below Director. Rewrite the compiler only if needed after fresh hash/read. Preserve provider-based AI path and schema validation.

### Gate 6 — AI Tests

Require arbitrary durations, deterministic output, requested feature coverage, 2D-only restraint, hybrid richness, tutorial/infographic semantics, and camera variety.

### Gate 7 — Studio UX

After render/AI contracts settle, add compact mobile authoring summaries for semantic coverage/fidelity and render profile. Browser-test desktop/mobile again.

### Gate 8 — Full Regression / Readback

Run Studio/shared movie/adapter/procedural/render tests, syntax, line limits, tabs, browser smoke, benchmark comparison. Re-read all touched files and write delta/evidence/handoff.

## Actual Candidate Files — Conditional Until Fresh Reads

New render files if benchmark supports child-process architecture:

- `apps/animator/tools/render/parallel/ParallelFrameProtocol.js`
- `apps/animator/tools/render/parallel/MalchusFrameWorker.js`
- `apps/animator/tools/render/parallel/TiferesRenderWorkerPool.js`
- `apps/animator/tools/render/parallel/YesodOrderedFrameBuffer.js`
- `apps/animator/tools/render/bench/ThreeMinuteRenderBenchmark.js`
- `apps/animator/tools/render/threeMinute/ThreeMinuteParallelExporter.js`

AI files are intentionally unnamed until current compiler readback; likely small modules under `apps/shared/movie/ai/planning/` plus a full rewrite of `MovieIntentCompiler.js` only if the current file remains the correct composition point.

Studio files are intentionally deferred until render/AI work proves new metadata/contracts worth displaying.

## Acceptance Thresholds

Render acceleration is successful only with identical frame hashes for compared timestamps and a material measured throughput gain under comparable load. AI improvement is successful only if generated canonical output contains requested semantic kinds/scene purpose/camera diversity rather than metadata promises. Studio improvement is successful only if mobile browser evidence shows the new information is usable without horizontal overflow or control loss.

No source work begins before `REMAINING_WORK.md` is written and current hot-path files are freshly read.
